title: A Real Bear Was a Corporal in the Polish Army

scenes.text: A real bear served in World War Two. As a corporal.
Polish soldiers adopted the cub in Iran in 1942 and named him Voytek.
Pets were banned on the ship to Italy. So they enlisted him. Private Voytek, with his own serial number.
At Monte Cassino in 1944, he carried ammunition crates on his hind legs. The soldiers said he never dropped one.
He loved beer and wrestling, so his unit put a bear carrying a shell on its badge.
He retired to Edinburgh Zoo. A corporal. Who was a bear.

description:
A real bear served in the Polish army in World War Two, and was promoted to corporal.
Wojtek, a Syrian brown bear adopted by the 22nd Artillery Supply Company in Iran in 1942, was formally enlisted so he could travel to Italy, carried ammunition crates during the Battle of Monte Cassino in 1944, and retired to Edinburgh Zoo, where he died in 1963.
Which animal would you want in your unit?
thumbnail_text: THE BEAR WHO WAS A SOLDIER
first_comment: Bonus: Wojtek was issued his own service number, pay book and cigarette allowance. He chewed the cigarettes. Which animal would you enlist?
